title: Cyprian (d. 258)
hookLine: you can't have God for your father without the Church for your mother; and the fight over welcoming back the lapsed

cards: The persecution is over, and the church in Carthage has a problem nobody prepared for. During it, an emperor's order told everyone to sacrifice to the gods. Some Christians refused, and suffered for it.
Some ran. And some gave in: they burned the incense, or bought a certificate saying they had. Now the danger has passed, and those who gave in are standing at the church door, asking to come home.
The bishop, Cyprian, has to answer them. So does everyone else.

teach.b: First, Cyprian's own position was awkward. When the persecution began, he went into hiding and led his people by letters. He said it was for their sake.
Some said he'd run. So when he speaks about those who fell, he isn't speaking from a pedestal. The church called them the lapsed, the fallen.
Second, two loud answers. Some of the confessors, Christians who had suffered and survived, wrote notes of peace welcoming the lapsed back at once, no questions asked.
At Rome, a priest named Novatian took the opposite line: those who had denied Christ could never be taken back by the Church.

Third, Cyprian's way: not at once, and not never. In his book On the Lapsed, he grieves over them. He asks for real repentance, time, and a decision by the bishops together, not a quick pardon from one person.
And then, a welcome home. Fourth, the picture behind it all.
In another book, On the Unity of the Church, he writes the line on today's screen, put simply: no one can have God for his Father who doesn't have the Church for his mother.
A mother can be strict. A mother also keeps the door open and sets a place at the table. For Cyprian, that was the Church: one family, holding the line and holding out its arms.
He died a martyr in the end. The account says that when the sentence was read, he answered: thanks be to God.

how: Catholics remember Saint Cyprian together with Pope Saint Cornelius in the Church's calendar, and both are named in the Roman Canon; the sacrament of penance is the Church's ordinary way of welcoming back those who have fallen.

games.q: you're a bishop. Christians who gave in under persecution want to come back. some say take them at once; some say never. what do you do?
o: take them back at once, no questions.
games.why: Cyprian chose neither extreme: real repentance, a decision by the bishops together, and then a welcome home.

practice: Think of someone who drifted away, from your family, your friends, your parish, or from you, and hold their face a moment, honestly, the hurt included if there is some.
Then ask what a first step back toward them would look like: not pretending nothing happened, just an open door. If you pray, hold them before God.

wordCard.voice: Cyprian. The bishop of Carthage who called the lapsed home through repentance, and said the Church is our mother. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the lapsed, the fallen — the name for Christians who gave in under persecution.

carryVoice: Your line: the Church is mother. Strict, and still setting a place at the table. Day seven hundred twelve, done.
